cards.explanation: The answer is that he starts crying out to Jesus. When he hears that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he begins to cry out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” (Mark 10:47). He calls Jesus by name and asks for mercy, out loud. No mumbling here, friends.
The word is silent. The text says many people admonished him to be silent (Mark 10:48). Admonished is a polite word for "hey, hush it." That's a lot of people telling one man to zip it, friends.

The answer is False. Many people admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder (Mark 10:48). He doesn't hush and he doesn't wait. I've had a few people tell me to quiet down in my day, and I did NOT handle it this well.

The answer is that Jesus stops and has him called over. The text says Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” (Mark 10:49). A large crowd is with Him, and still He stops. Then He has Bartimaeus called over, friends.

The answer is take courage and get up. They called the blind man and said, “Take courage!” and “Get up! He is calling for you.” (Mark 10:49). Jesus is the one calling for him, and those words carry the news. Good news deserves a little cheering, bakers.

The answer is True. The text says, “Throwing off his cloak, Bartimaeus jumped up and came to Jesus.” (Mark 10:50). He throws off his cloak and he JUMPS. I wish I moved like that when my oven timer goes off, friends.
The word is see. Bartimaeus says, “Rabboni, let me see again.” (Mark 10:51). Jesus asked what he wanted, and Bartimaeus tells Him plainly. He asks to see again, friends.
The answer is False. Mark 10:52 says, “And immediately he received his sight…” There's no waiting period, bakers. Jesus speaks, and Bartimaeus can see.

The answer is that he follows Jesus along the road. The text says he “…followed Jesus along the road.” (Mark 10:52). Jesus told him, “Go,” and he could see, so he went the same way Jesus was going. I think that says a lot, but I'll let you chew on it, friends.
